name: rustic cobbled work yard ground autotile: rounded warm river cobbles with dark earth joints, a low dressed stone kerb rim with a 2px front face on the south edge, grass tufts at the rim, lying flat on grass (top-down 3/4 RPG ground)
label: beodeul_yard/cobble

surfaces.part: cobble ground field (flat top-down cobbles with dark joints)
dressed stone kerb rim with 2px south front face

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile: a large cobble field seen from above with a thin stone kerb outline. Only the south kerb has a front face, and it is about 2 rows (rows 138-139, lighter edge over a darker row). That is under the 3-row minimum for a front face, so I read the whole piece as a flat top-down slab, not a 3/4 volume. Grass tufts sit on the rim. There is no receding side face and no cap.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 16 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 3%, so there are no large flat fills. Cobbles are shaded one by one in warm tan, brown and grey, with dark earth joints between them. The 0% near-neutral share of dark edge pixels means the outlines are tinted, not black. They read as dark brown earth tones next to the cobbles and a light dressed stone kerb with a 2px south face. Grass tufts sit at the rim. Only the surrounding grass is plain, and it carries speckle texture comparable to the grass reference. The cobble ramps have roughly 5 steps. The candidate is at or above the references on every primary fact, with no sticker-like outline.

surfaces.part: dressed stone kerb front face on south edges

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile and not a standing object. The cobble field covers nearly all rows, with dark earth joints in the column scans (L=38 to 79) and light cobble highlights (L=118 to 215). The only vertical face is the pale kerb strip on the south edges, which is 2 rows tall (for example the pale rows 34-35 at x=131 sit just above the dark joint line). That is under the 3-row minimum for a front face, so the tile measures as a flat slab with a thin kerb lip. There is no receding side face, no roof or ellipse, and no eave shadow. The green hole in the middle and the rim tufts are decor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The cobbles are shaded one by one in warm tan, brown and grey, each with a light top and a dark underside, set in dark brown earth joints. That gives about 5 steps on the cobble ramp, and the kerb adds light top, mid face and dark base steps. The measured facts agree: 16 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference, and only 3% near-flat coverage. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean brown or green, which makes them dark_material_tone rather than a black sticker line. The kerb rim reads as dressed stone with a 2px south face, and there are small grass tufts along the rim. The surrounding grass is fairly quiet, with only faint tufting, but it is comparable to the reference grass and has no large flat blocks. Overall the piece is at or above the reference in richness and structure.

surfaces.part: dressed stone kerb rim, south edge front face

answer.evidence: The tile is a flat, camera-facing ground autotile. The cobble field with dark joints fills almost the whole shape and is drawn straight top-down with no foreshortening. The only vertical element is the pale stone kerb. Its south front face is just 2 rows (a light kerb line over a dark outline) wherever the patch ends on its south edge, for example around the central grass hole and the bottom steps. No receding side face is drawn. Because the front face is under 3 rows, it reads as a top-down slab. This is expected for a terrain tile with a thin kerb lip.

styleAnswer.evidence: The cobbles are shaded one by one in warm browns, greys and tans, with dark earth joints between them. That reads as roughly 5 lightness steps. The measured 16 visible tones per tile is well above the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 3%, against 0% for the references, so there are no flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines and joints lean brown and are tinted rather than a black sticker line. The stone kerb rim has a lighter top face and a darker south face, and the grass tufts at the rim fit the references. The surrounding grass carries a faint tuft texture comparable to the grass reference. Structure and shading craft are at the Beodeul bar.

surfaces.part: cobble ground field with dark earth joints
dressed stone kerb rim, south edge front face
surfaces.rows: on the south edge of each cobble region, 2 rows (e.g. 140-141)

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile seen from above. The cobble field is a large horizontal surface with a thin stone kerb outline. The only vertical face is the 2-row kerb front on the south edge, which is under the 3 rows needed for a front face. The grass-colored hole in the middle also has a thin kerb. No standing volume is drawn: there is no tall front face, no eave and no side face. By the view contract this reads as a top-down slab. As terrain, that is the expected form for flat ground.

styleAnswer.evidence: The cobbles are shaded one by one in several tones (grey, tan, warm brown) with highlights and dark earth joints between them. That is the stone-by-stone treatment Beodeul uses, and it is denser than the reference paving. The measured facts agree: 16 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving and 3 for the grass, and only 3% near-flat coverage. The 0% neutral dark edge pixels mean the joints and kerb shadows are tinted brown, not a black sticker line. The pale dressed-stone kerb has a visible 2px south face, and there are small grass tufts at the rim. The surrounding grass carries a faint tuft pattern and is not a flat fill. The kerb is a little uniform and the grass is subtler than the reference grass, but a careful artist would accept this next to the references.
